verses.en:
Master Sun said:
Arms are the gravest business of a state:
the ground on which men live or die,
the path by which a nation stands or falls.
Of this, nothing may be left unweighed.
verses.living: Some decisions are not like the others: a move abroad, a marriage, staking your savings on a business. Sunzi's first word is to recognise which matters carry this weight. Give them slow, careful attention, not the quick reflex we give to email. Name your few great matters this year and refuse to decide them casually.

Before a launch or a negotiation, run it through a fixed checklist rather than through your mood that morning. The same five questions, asked the same way each time, expose what enthusiasm hides. A framework is not bureaucracy; it is a mirror that refuses to flatter.

verses.en:
The Way is what makes the people
of one mind with those above,
so that they will die with them,
live with them,
and not flinch at danger.
verses.living: A team that shares the purpose will carry a project through a bad quarter; a team that merely obeys will scatter at the first storm. Before asking anyone, a colleague or a teenager, to endure hardship alongside you, ask whether they truly share the why. Spend more time on alignment than on instruction.

verses.en:
Heaven is yin and yang,
cold and heat,
the measure of the seasons.
Earth is far and near,
rugged and easy,
open and narrow,
ground of death and ground of life.
verses.living: Every plan sits inside conditions you did not choose. Think of the season of the market, the energy of your year, the terrain of your industry or your family. Timing and ground are not excuses but facts to be read. Ask of any venture: is this the season, and is this the place to stand?

verses.en:
The commander is wisdom and good faith,
humanity, courage and strictness.
Method is the ordering of units,
the duties of officers,
the governing of supply.
verses.living: Notice that humanity and strictness sit side by side in Sunzi's list. A parent or manager who is kind but never firm, or firm but never kind, holds only half the set. And method, who does what and where the money goes, is not dull detail; it is where good intentions turn into results.

Most of us have heard the basics: sleep, save, prepare, listen. The gap lies between having heard and knowing, between reciting a principle and living by it. Pick one rule you could lecture on and check honestly whether your week reflects it.

verses.en:
So compare them by reckoning
and search out how things truly stand. Ask:
Which ruler has the Way?
Which commander has the ability?
Who holds the advantages of Heaven and Earth?
Whose laws and orders are carried out?
Whose forces are stronger?
Whose soldiers are better trained?
Whose rewards and punishments are clear?
By these I know who will win and who will lose.
verses.living: Seven plain questions, asked of both sides, will tell you more than hope can. Before applying for a role or bidding for a contract, answer them for yourself and for the competition. Who is better led, better prepared, more disciplined, clearer about what they reward. If the answers trouble you, you have learned something cheaply.

verses.en:
A commander who heeds my reckoning,
employed, will surely win: keep him.
A commander who ignores my reckoning,
employed, will surely lose: send him away.
Once the reckoning favours us and is heeded,
build shi, momentum,
to carry it beyond the plan.
Shi is this:
moving with what is advantageous,
you take hold of the scales.
verses.living: Planning at the desk is half the work; the other half is acting on a shifting balance once you are out in the world. Keep near you people who actually listen, and once the plan is sound, stop deliberating and build momentum. Then stay alert: momentum means adjusting to advantage as it appears, not clinging to the script.

Read as wisdom rather than trickery, this is about not showing your hand too early. A writer need not announce the novel before it exists; a job-seeker need not reveal every option at the first interview. Learn too to see through others' displays: the buyer who seems indifferent may be the most eager.

Turn this list around and use it as a mirror: each line names a weakness by which you yourself can be moved. Greed, disorder, temper, vanity, fatigue and a rift with a friend are exactly the handles a pushy salesperson or a rival reaches for. Know which handle you carry most visibly, and keep it out of reach.

verses.en:
Strike where they are unready;
emerge where they do not look.
These are the strategist's victories,
and they cannot be told beforehand.
verses.living: The opening you need often lies where no one is looking: the neglected market, the unfashionable skill, the quiet hour before others wake. Such chances cannot be scripted from afar; they are seen only on the ground, in the moment. Prepare thoroughly, then trust yourself to improvise.

verses.en:
Whoever wins the temple reckoning before battle
has more counting rods on his side;
whoever loses the temple reckoning before battle
has fewer.
More counts win, fewer counts lose,
and how much worse to have no count at all!
Looking at it this way,
I can see who will win and who will lose.
verses.living: Outcomes are usually settled at the kitchen table before they show in the world: in the budget, the training plan, the rehearsal. The worst position is not a poor calculation but none at all. Before any important move, sit down and count on paper what is for you and what is against.

verses.en:
Master Sun said:
In all the business of arms,
with a thousand swift chariots,
a thousand leather-armoured wagons,
a hundred thousand in mail,
and grain hauled a thousand li,
the costs at home and in the field,
the keep of envoys and guests,
glue and lacquer for repairs,
the upkeep of chariots and armour,
come to a thousand pieces of gold a day.
Only then can a hundred thousand take the field.
verses.living: Every serious undertaking has a daily burn rate, whether it is a start-up, a renovation or a lawsuit. Sunzi lists even the glue and lacquer: the small costs that quietly add up. Before you begin, write the real daily cost of the project, including what nobody budgets for, such as time, attention and goodwill.

verses.en:
When you fight, seek victory.
Drag it out, and weapons dull, edges blunt;
besiege a city, and your strength is spent;
keep the army long in the field,
and the state's resources fall short.
When weapons are dull and edges blunt,
strength drained and treasure gone,
neighbouring lords rise to profit from your exhaustion,
and even the wisest
cannot then mend what follows.
verses.living: Long fights wear down even the side that is right: a dispute with a neighbour, a project that never ships, a feud with a sibling. While you are spent, others take their chance. Decide early what a reasonable ending looks like, and close the matter before it closes you.

verses.en:
So we have heard of clumsy haste in war,
but never seen cleverness that lingers.
No state has ever profited from a long war.
Whoever does not fully grasp the harm of arms
cannot fully grasp their use.
verses.living: Done roughly and soon often beats done perfectly and late: ship the first version, send the imperfect apology, make the call today. Endless polishing is its own kind of defeat. And understand the downside of any tool, whether credit, conflict or ambition, before you trust yourself with its upside.

verses.en:
One skilled in arms
does not levy troops a second time
nor ship provisions a third.
Bring your equipment from home,
forage your grain from the enemy,
and the army will have enough to eat.
verses.living: Raise resources once, then make the work feed itself: a side business that funds its own growth, a habit that rewards itself. Repeated appeals for more money, more time and more patience are a sign the design is wrong. Ask how the venture can supply what it consumes.

Costs compound: a long commute drains money and then energy, and the drained energy makes everything else dearer. Find the chain in your own life where one strain feeds the next, and break it at the first link. Moving closer to work, clearing one debt or dropping one draining commitment can lift several burdens at once.

verses.en:
Strength spent, wealth exhausted,
households in the heartland stand empty.
Of the people's means,
seven parts in ten are gone.
Of the state's,
broken chariots, worn-out horses,
helmets, armour, arrows and crossbows,
halberds, shields and great mantlets,
oxen and heavy wagons,
six parts in ten are gone.
verses.living: Sunzi does the arithmetic of exhaustion: most of the cost of a long struggle is invisible at the start. Before entering a drawn-out conflict at work or in the family, picture the inventory afterwards: what friendships, health and savings will be left standing? If the answer is four parts in ten, look for another way.

verses.en:
So the wise commander takes pains to feed on the enemy.
One measure of their grain
is worth twenty of ours;
one bale of their fodder
worth twenty of our own.
verses.living: Use what the situation already provides rather than carrying everything from home. A competitor's public mistakes are free lessons; a critic's objection is raw material for your next draft. Knowledge gathered in the field is worth twenty times what you haul in from theory.

verses.en:
What drives men to kill the foe is anger;
what draws them to seize his goods is reward.
In chariot fighting, when ten or more chariots are taken,
reward the first to capture one,
change the banners,
mix the captured chariots among our own,
treat the captured soldiers well and keep them.
This is called defeating the enemy and growing stronger.
verses.living: People need both a fire and a share: a reason to care and a part in what is won. Reward the first person who takes a risk. When newcomers join from a rival firm or another school, make them truly yours: new colours, a real welcome, good treatment. A victory that honours the former opponent makes you stronger; one that humiliates breeds new enemies.

verses.en:
So in war, prize victory,
not duration.
The commander who understands war
holds the people's fate in his hands;
on him rests the safety or the peril of the state.
verses.living: Value the result, not the hours spent or the length of the struggle. Whoever leads, a parent, a manager, a founder, carries others' fortunes and should feel that weight as a reason to finish things well and swiftly. Long effort is not a virtue in itself; a good outcome is.

In a dispute, the best outcome usually leaves the other side, and the relationship, intact. Win a negotiation by breaking a supplier, or an argument by crushing a partner, and you own the ruins. From the largest matter to the smallest, aim to win the thing whole.

verses.en:
So a hundred victories in a hundred battles
is not the summit of skill.
To bend the enemy's army without a battle:
that is the summit of skill.
verses.living: The best manager settles the conflict before it becomes a meeting; the best parent shapes the evening so the tantrum never comes. Winning every argument is a sign you are having too many arguments. Seek the arrangement that makes the fight unnecessary.

When something stands in your way, meet it at the earliest level. Start with the intention, then the relationships, then the conduct, and only last the entrenched position. If a colleague is set on a poor plan, engage the thinking behind it long before you are reduced to fighting a finished decision. Frontal assaults on fortified positions are where most energy is wasted.

verses.en:
Building shields and siege carts
and readying engines takes three months;
heaping the earthen ramps
takes three months more.
If the commander, unable to master his anger,
sends his men swarming up the walls like ants,
a third of them are killed
and still the city stands.
This is the calamity of siege.
verses.living: Anger makes us storm walls: the furious email, the all-out confrontation, the doubling down on a failing bet. The usual price is a third of your strength and nothing to show for it. When you feel the urge to swarm the wall, put the decision off until the heat has passed.

verses.en:
So one skilled in arms
bends armies without battle,
takes cities without siege,
brings down states without long campaigns.
He contends for all under heaven by keeping things whole,
so his troops are not worn down
and the gain is complete.
This is the method of attacking by stratagem.
verses.living: Look for the route that wins without spending you. It might be an offer so good the rival becomes a partner, a habit so easy it needs no willpower. The aim is gain without wreckage, so that your energy and your relationships are still there tomorrow. Before any campaign, ask whether a whole victory is available.

Match your approach to your real strength. A small firm that fights the giant head-on is simply swallowed; one that slips into a niche survives. In a household budget or a career, know when your position lets you push. Know when it calls for patience, and when it is wise to step aside without shame.

The people nearest the centre of any enterprise, a deputy, a co-founder, a spouse, are its frame. Where trust between them is tight, the whole holds; where there are gaps, everything rattles. Tend that closeness deliberately.

verses.en:
A ruler can bring harm on his army in three ways.
Not knowing the army cannot advance,
he orders it forward;
not knowing the army cannot retreat,
he orders it back.
This is called hobbling the army.
verses.living: Leaders who are far from the work yet insist on steering it make the most expensive mistakes. If you manage people, ask before you order: can this actually move right now? If you are managed this way, bring the ground truth to the person deciding, clearly and early.

verses.en:
Not knowing the army's affairs,
yet meddling in its administration,
he leaves the officers bewildered.
Not knowing the army's weighing of circumstance,
yet meddling in its command,
he leaves the officers in doubt.
Once the army is bewildered and in doubt,
trouble from the neighbouring lords arrives.
This is called unsettling your own army
and handing away the victory.
verses.living: Two voices giving orders breed confusion; authority without understanding breeds doubt. Parents who overrule each other in front of the children create exactly this. Decide who holds which responsibility, then let them hold it.

verses.en:
So there are five ways to foreknow victory.
Who knows when to fight and when not to fight will win.
Who knows how to use both large and small forces will win.
Where high and low want the same, they will win.
Who waits, prepared, for the unprepared will win.
Whose commander is able and not reined in by the ruler will win.
These five are the way to foreknow victory.
verses.living: Read this as a checklist for any shared effort: a house move, a product launch, a family holiday. Is this the right fight? Can we work at the right scale? Do we all want the same thing? Are we readier than the problem? Does the person in charge have room to act? Five honest yeses predict success better than talent does.

verses.en:
So it is said:
know them, know yourself,
and a hundred battles bring no peril.
Know yourself but not them,
and you win one, lose one.
Know neither them nor yourself,
and every battle is mortal danger.
verses.living: Most failures come from seeing only half the picture. In a hard conversation, know your own triggers and also what the other person fears. In a career move, know your strengths and also what the employer truly needs. Self-knowledge alone gives even odds; add understanding of the other, and you are seldom in danger.

verses.en:
Master Sun said:
those of old who were good at war
first made themselves unbeatable,
then waited for the enemy to become beatable.

Being unbeatable rests with us;
being beatable rests with them.
So the skilled can make themselves unconquerable,
but cannot make the enemy sure to fall.

Hence the saying:
victory can be known,
it cannot be made.
verses.living: Your part is to remove your own weaknesses; whether a chance appears is partly up to the world. Before a job interview, a launch or a hard conversation, put your energy into what you control: preparation, rest, clarity. Then watch for the opening without trying to manufacture it.

When resources are thin, guard and consolidate; when they overflow, go forward. A small business in a lean year should protect cash and customers, not open a second shop. Know which season you are in, and commit fully to the posture it calls for, whether that is lying low or moving boldly.

verses.en:
To see a victory only when everyone can see it
is not the best of the best.
To win in battle and have the whole world cry 'well done'
is not the best of the best.

Lifting an autumn hair is no sign of strength;
seeing sun and moon, no sign of sharp eyes;
hearing thunder, no sign of keen ears.
verses.living: Real foresight notices what others have not yet noticed: the early sign of burnout in a colleague, the small cost that will compound. Applause is a poor measure of skill. The deepest competence often goes unseen because it dealt with the problem before it became visible.

verses.en:
Those the ancients called skilled in war
won where winning was easy.
So their victories brought
no fame for wisdom,
no merit for courage.

Their battles were won without error;
without error, because all they set in place
was bound to win:
they conquered those already defeated.
verses.living: Arrange things so that the decisive moment is easy. A writer who drafts a little every morning finishes the book without heroics. A household that automates savings never needs willpower at the end of the month. If success looks dull from outside, you probably built it well.

verses.en:
So the skilled take their stand on ground where they cannot lose,
and do not miss the moment the enemy can.

The victorious army wins first, then seeks battle;
the defeated army fights first, then looks for a way to win.

The one who uses troops well
cultivates the Way and keeps to method,
and so holds in hand
the government of victory and defeat.
verses.living: Before you pitch the client, ask for the raise or enter the negotiation, the outcome should already be largely settled. Your research, your alternatives and your relationships settle it. People who walk in hoping to improvise a win usually lose. Tend the basics, your values and your systems, and results begin to answer to you.

Good decisions run on a chain of honest measurement. Thinking of moving city for work? Measure the ground (costs, commute, family), estimate what you need, count what you have, weigh the two side by side. Victory is the last link, never the first.

verses.en:
So a winning army is like a heavy weight set against a grain;
a losing army, like a grain set against a weight.

When the victor sends his people into battle
it is like bursting a dam of gathered water
into a gorge a thousand fathoms deep:
this is form.
verses.living: Accumulate quietly until the balance is overwhelming, then release all at once. A musician who has practised a piece for months plays it with ease on the night. A team that has rehearsed a launch lets it go like water through a gate. The force was stored long before it was seen.

verses.en:
Master Sun said:
to govern many as you govern few
is a matter of division and number;
to fight with many as you fight with few
is a matter of signals, form and name.

That the whole host may take the enemy's blow
and never be broken:
this is the unexpected and the orthodox.
That an army falls on its target
like a whetstone thrown at an egg:
this is empty and full.
verses.living: Growth is manageable only with structure. A team of fifty can move like a team of five if roles are divided clearly and signals are simple. Before you expand, a family budget, a club or a company, decide how it will be split and how people will know what to do.

verses.en:
In all battle,
join with the orthodox,
win with the unexpected.

One who is good at the unexpected
is boundless as heaven and earth,
unending as rivers and seas;
ending and beginning again,
like sun and moon;
dying and coming back to life,
like the four seasons.
verses.living: Show up with the solid, expected work, then let the original touch decide the matter. In a job application, the competent CV gets you into the room; the one unusual project or question is what people remember. Keep a store of fresh ideas that renews itself, like seasons, by reading and wandering widely.

verses.en:
There are no more than five notes,
yet their changes are more than ear can hear.
There are no more than five colours,
yet their changes are more than eye can see.
There are no more than five tastes,
yet their changes are more than tongue can know.

In battle there are only two forces, surprise and the expected,
yet their changes are more than mind can exhaust.
Each gives birth to the other,
a ring that has no end.
Who could ever exhaust them?
verses.living: You do not need endless resources to be inventive; a few elements in fresh combinations are enough. A cook with five ingredients, a designer with three colours, a parent with a handful of games can keep things new for years. When you feel stuck, recombine what you have rather than waiting for something new.

verses.en:
The rush of a torrent
that sweeps away boulders:
that is force.
The swoop of a hawk
that breaks its prey:
that is timing.

So the skilled in war
make their force steep
and their timing short.
Force is the crossbow drawn full;
timing, the release of the trigger.
verses.living: Power has two parts: the pressure you build and the instant you let it go. A salesperson builds trust over weeks, then makes the request in one clear sentence. Do not dribble your energy out in half measures; gather it, then strike once and cleanly.

What looks messy from outside, a busy kitchen, a household with young children, a startup in launch week, can be deeply ordered inside. Equally, apparent weakness can be a deliberate posture. Courage is rarely a fixed trait; it rises and falls with the situation, so arrange situations that make bravery easier for yourself and others.

People respond to what they are shown and offered. Read this as a lesson in seeing through others' bait: the free trial, the flattering offer, the 'limited time' deal. And in your own work, lead with genuine benefit, then be ready when people come towards it.

verses.en:
So the skilled in war
seek it in the force of configuration
and do not lay the burden on people;
they can choose their people
and trust to the configuration.

One who trusts to configuration
sends people into battle
like rolling logs and stones.
It is the nature of logs and stones
to rest on level ground and move on a slope,
to stop when square
and roll when round.
verses.living: When results disappoint, look first at the setup, not at the person. A child who will not do homework may need a quiet table and a set hour, not a lecture. A team missing deadlines may need clearer priorities, not more pressure. Design the slope and people will roll.

verses.en:
So the force of those who are skilled at war
is like a round stone rolled
down a mountain a thousand fathoms high:
that is shì.
verses.living: The hard work is getting the stone to the top and making it round; after that, a touch is enough. Spend most of your effort on position: skills, relationships, reputation. Then a single small push, an email, a proposal, a call, can carry enormous weight.

verses.en:
Master Sun said:
whoever reaches the field first and waits for the enemy
is at ease;
whoever arrives late and hurries into battle
is worn out.

So the skilled in war
bring others to them
and are not brought.
verses.living: Being early is a strategy. Arrive before the meeting, start the project before the deadline looms, prepare before the talk with your teenager. When you have set the ground and the pace, you can meet others calmly while they hurry to catch up.

People move towards benefit and away from cost; design your proposals with that in mind, honestly. And the easiest road is often through empty country: the niche nobody serves, the skill few bother to learn. A career built where competition is thin can travel very far without exhaustion.

verses.en:
To take what you attack, attack what is not defended;
to hold what you defend, defend what will not be attacked.

So against the good attacker
the enemy does not know what to defend;
against the good defender
the enemy does not know what to attack.

Subtle, so subtle,
reaching formlessness;
mysterious, so mysterious,
reaching soundlessness.
So he becomes master of the enemy's fate.
verses.living: Do not announce every plan before it is ready. A founder who keeps the next product quiet, or a negotiator who does not reveal her walk-away point, keeps room to move. Discretion is not dishonesty; it is simply not handing others the map before the journey.

verses.en:
Advance and no one can resist, if you strike at the empty;
withdraw and no one can follow, if you are too swift to be caught.

So when I want battle,
though the enemy sits behind high walls and deep moats,
he must come out,
for I strike what he must save.

When I do not want battle,
though I hold only a line drawn on the ground,
he cannot engage me,
for I turn him aside from his course.
verses.living: Influence comes from touching what matters most to the other side. In a stalled negotiation, address the concern they cannot ignore, their deadline or their reputation, and they will come to the table. And when you wish to avoid a pointless quarrel, a light redirection often works better than a wall.

verses.en:
Make the enemy show his form while you remain formless,
and you are concentrated while he is divided.
I am one; he is split into ten.
Then it is ten against one,
and I am many where he is few.

If I can strike the few with the many,
those I fight are already in straits.

Where I will fight must not be known.
Unknown, the enemy must guard many places;
guarding many, those I meet at any one
are few.
verses.living: Concentration is the great multiplier. If you spread your week across ten goals you meet each one with a tenth of yourself; choose one and you bring all of it. A student revising one subject deeply each day outperforms one who skims everything at once.

You cannot defend against every possible criticism, risk or rival. A product that tries to please every user pleases none deeply. A person who tries to avoid every disapproval ends up with no shape at all. Decide what you will leave unguarded, and put your strength where it counts.

verses.en:
Know the place of battle,
know the day of battle,
and you may march a thousand miles to meet it.

Know neither the place nor the day,
and the left cannot help the right,
the right cannot help the left,
the front cannot help the rear,
the rear cannot help the front,

how much less when they lie tens of miles apart,
or even a few?
verses.living: Clear time and place turn scattered people into a coordinated force. A family reunion, a product launch or a group trip falls apart without a fixed date and venue. Name the when and the where early, and others can travel any distance to meet you there.

Size alone does not decide outcomes; understanding does. Before you face a large competitor or a daunting exam, probe: try a small test, ask a question, run a pilot. Each light touch tells you where the strength is thick and where it runs thin.

verses.en:
So the height of giving an army form
is to reach formlessness.
Formless, the deepest spy cannot peer in,
the wisest cannot lay plans against you.

Victory is placed before the crowd according to form,
and the crowd cannot grasp it.
Everyone sees the shape by which I won;
no one sees the shape by which I shaped the win.

So no victory is repeated:
each answers form with form, without end.
verses.living: Others will copy what you did; they rarely see how you decided to do it. Rather than repeating last year's winning formula, keep the underlying way of thinking and let the outward form change. A teacher who reads each class freshly never runs out of lessons.

verses.en:
An army's form is like water.
Water's form avoids the heights and runs to the low;
an army's form avoids the full and strikes the empty.

Water shapes its flow by the ground;
an army shapes its victory by the enemy.

So an army has no constant force,
water no constant shape.
One who can win by changing with the enemy
is called divine.
verses.living: Flow towards openings and around obstacles rather than through them. If a door at work is firmly closed, find the one that is ajar: another team, another format, another season. Rigidity breaks; responsiveness keeps moving, and over time it carves its own course.

Nothing holds the upper hand for ever: not your rival, not your slump, not your winning streak. Hold good times lightly and hard times patiently. Change is the one constant, and it is the friend of anyone who keeps adapting.

verses.en:
Sunzi said:
In every use of arms
the general takes his charge from the sovereign,
musters the host, draws the many together,
and pitches camp face to face with the foe;
and of all this nothing is harder
than the contest for advantage.
And the hardness is this:
to make the winding road the straight one,
to turn misfortune into gain.
verses.living: Most of any venture is assembly: people, budget, plan. The real test comes when you must reach the decisive point before others, and the obvious road is jammed. Of any setback this week, ask: is there a longer way round that actually arrives sooner?

verses.en:
So lengthen your own route
and lure the other on with a bait of gain;
set out after him,
arrive before him.
This is one who knows the reckoning
of the crooked and the straight.
verses.living: When a rival rushes for the obvious prize, let them spend themselves on it while you take the quieter road to what matters. Someone who spends a month building a real portfolio often overtakes the applicants who fired off a hundred forms on the first day.

Every push for speed has its price. Carry everything and you are too slow; strip down too far and you lose what sustains you. Before a launch sprint, decide plainly what must travel with you and what can safely wait.

verses.en:
So if men roll up their armour and run,
resting neither day nor night,
marching double stages without a halt,
to contend for gain a hundred li off,
all three commanders will be taken:
the strong in front, the weary trailing,
and by this rule one in ten arrives.
At fifty li, the leading general stumbles,
and half arrive.
At thirty li, two in three arrive.
verses.living: Forced marches look heroic and leave most of the team behind. The farther the goal, the more ruinous the rush. A month of late nights aimed at a distant deadline usually delivers a fraction of the people and of the quality. Shorten the distance or ease the pace; do not pretend you can do neither.

Supply is never glamorous, but it is what lets anything last. Keep some months of expenses saved, keep sleep and meals regular through a hard season, keep your tools in repair. Ambition without provisions simply runs out.

verses.en:
Who does not know the designs of the neighbouring lords
cannot make alliances in good time.
Who does not know the shape of mountain and forest,
of gorge and pass, of marsh and fen,
cannot march an army.
Who will not use local guides
cannot win the advantage of the ground.
verses.living: Before moving into a new field, learn who is already there and what they want, study the terrain, and ask someone who lives there. In a new job, the most valuable hour of the first week may be a coffee. Have it with the person who has done the work for ten years.

Not every moment calls for the same tempo. In a negotiation there is a time to sit still and say little. There is a time to let the other side wonder, and a time to commit fully and fast. Learn all six speeds, and keep your plans to yourself until the thunder.

verses.en:
When you take the countryside, share among your people;
when you widen your ground, share out the gains.
Hang the matter on the balance, then move.
Whoever first knows the reckoning
of the crooked and the straight will win.
This is the method of the race for advantage.
verses.living: When a venture succeeds, share the rewards with those who carried it; a team that profits together stays together. And before each move, put the options on the scales: weighing first is what lets you move cleanly afterwards.

verses.en:
The Book of Army Administration says:
'Where voices cannot carry, we make gongs and drums;
where eyes cannot reach, we make banners and flags.'
Gongs and drums, banners and flags
make the ears and eyes of the people one.
Once they are one,
the brave cannot press on alone,
the fearful cannot fall back alone.
This is the art of moving the many.
verses.living: A team needs shared signals more than lone heroes. Give it a steady weekly rhythm, a board everyone can see, a few agreed words for stop and go. When everyone sees and hears the same thing, the eager do not run off and the anxious do not quietly drift away.

Choose the channel to suit the conditions. A team scattered across time zones, working in one another's dark, needs clear written notes. A team in one room needs a whiteboard all can see. A message that does not reach the senses has not been sent.

verses.en:
A whole army can be robbed of its spirit;
a general can be robbed of his heart.
Morning spirit is keen,
midday spirit flags,
evening spirit turns toward home.
The skilled commander avoids the keen spirit
and strikes the slack and the homeward.
This is mastery of qi.
verses.living: Energy has tides, your own and other people's. Do your hardest thinking while you are fresh. Raise a difficult subject with your partner neither when they are bristling nor when they are spent, but in the settled hour. Track your own daily curve for a week and plan around it.

In a heated meeting, the calm person who has slept and eaten usually settles the outcome. Prepare your own state before you meet someone else's storm. And when the opposition is plainly strong and well ordered, wait: conditions always shift.

Some contests should never be entered. Do not argue uphill against a deeply held conviction, do not chase an offer that looks too easy. When someone is cornered in a dispute, leave them a dignified way out. People with no exit fight hardest; people offered a graceful door often walk through it.

verses.en:
Sunzi said:
In every use of arms
the general takes his charge from the sovereign
and gathers the many into an army.
verses.living: Every mandate begins with someone else's instructions and a group to be brought together. Receiving the brief is the start of responsibility, not its end: what follows is your own judgement about how to carry it out.

verses.en:
On broken ground, do not camp.
Where highways cross, join hands with allies.
On cut-off ground, do not linger.
On hemmed-in ground, use stratagem.
On deadly ground, fight.
There are roads not to be travelled,
armies not to be struck,
cities not to be besieged,
ground not to be contested,
and commands of the sovereign
not to be obeyed.
verses.living: Different situations ask for different moves. Part of wisdom is the list of things you will not do: the opportunities you decline, the quarrels you do not join. A good manager will sometimes set aside an instruction from above. Those closest to the problem can see what head office cannot. Then the manager must own that choice openly.

verses.en:
The general who grasps the uses of the nine variations
knows how to wield arms.
The general who does not
may know the lie of the land
and still win nothing from it.
Whoever commands troops without the art of variation,
though he knows the five advantages,
cannot turn them to account.
verses.living: Knowledge without adaptability is a map without legs. You can know every principle of budgeting and still fall into debt if you cannot adjust when your income changes. Practise applying what you know to the situation in front of you, not the one in the textbook.

verses.en:
So the thinking of the wise
always mingles gain and harm.
Mingle harm into thoughts of gain,
and the work can be trusted;
mingle gain into thoughts of harm,
and trouble can be untied.
verses.living: When an offer excites you, list what could go wrong; when a setback flattens you, list what it makes possible. A job offer looks different after an honest page of drawbacks, and a redundancy looks different after an honest page of openings.

People move for three reasons: to avoid loss, because they are kept busy, and toward reward. Understand this chiefly so that you can see it working on you. Notice which commitments you keep from fear, which from mere busyness, and which because you truly want what they bring.

Hope is not a plan. Do not count on the boiler holding, the client staying, the illness passing you by. Count on the emergency fund, the second client, the daily walk. Build the position that does not depend on luck.

verses.en:
A general has five dangers.
Bent on dying, he can be killed.
Bent on living, he can be captured.
Quick to anger, he can be goaded by insult.
Jealous of his honour, he can be shamed.
Tender toward his people, he can be harried.
verses.living: Each danger is a virtue overextended: courage, prudence, passion, integrity, care. Know which is yours. If you cannot bear to look bad, anyone who threatens your reputation can steer you. If you cannot bear to disappoint anyone, you will be run ragged.

verses.en:
These five are the general's failings
and the ruin of any campaign.
When an army is overturned and its general slain,
the cause lies always among the five dangers.
They must be examined.
verses.living: Most collapses trace back not to the market or the rival but to a flaw in the person at the centre. Once a season, ask someone who knows you well which of your strengths has begun to work against you.

chapters.title_en: On the March: Reading the Signs

verses.living: When you enter difficult territory, stay close to your sources of supply. Keep your outlook sunward and your footing high, and never begin an argument from below. Starting a small business, choose a valley where water runs: customers, suppliers, people who can help.

verses.en:
Having crossed a river, move well away from it.
When an invader crosses toward you,
do not meet him in midstream;
let half his force reach the bank, then strike:
there is your advantage.
If you mean to fight, do not hug the water to meet him.
Camp facing the light, on high ground,
and never face upstream against the current.
So much for armies by rivers.
verses.living: Transitions are where everyone is most exposed: halfway through a house move, a reorganisation, a new system. Do not linger in your own crossings; finish them and get clear of the bank. And try not to take on big commitments while you are still midstream.

verses.en:
Cross salt marshes quickly, and do not stay.
If you must fight in the middle of a marsh,
keep to the water and the grasses
with a stand of trees at your back.
So much for armies in the salt marsh.
verses.living: Some seasons are simply bad ground: a corrosive workplace, a draining habit, a spiral of debt. Get through them fast rather than settling in. If you must stay a while, find the small sources of nourishment and something solid to lean against.

verses.en:
On the level plain, take open, easy ground
with the heights to your right and rear,
death before you and life behind.
So much for armies on the plain.
These four advantages of position
are how the Yellow Emperor overcame the four emperors.
verses.living: Even on easy ground, arrange what stands behind you: savings, health, the people who have your back. Then you can face the hard thing in front with a clear mind. A negotiator with a good alternative in reserve can afford to stay calm in the room.

verses.en:
An army loves the heights and hates the hollows,
prizes the sunlit side and shuns the shade;
it tends its life and keeps to solid ground,
free of the hundred ills:
this is called sure victory.
On hills and dykes, hold the sunny face
with the slope at your right and rear.
This is the profit of arms, the help of the ground.
verses.living: Health is strategy. Light, fresh air, firm footing and good food spare a household or a team a hundred small illnesses, and that alone carries it far. Move your desk to the window, open the curtains, and notice how much of strategy is plain well-being.

verses.en:
When it has rained upstream
and foam comes riding down,
if you would ford,
wait until it settles.
verses.living: When the signs say a surge is coming, a swing in the markets, someone's temper rising, a flood of news, do not wade in. Wait for the water to settle. Many bad decisions are simply good decisions made a day too early.

verses.en:
Where the land has sheer ravines,
Heaven's Wells and Heaven's Prisons,
Heaven's Nets, Heaven's Pitfalls, Heaven's Clefts,
leave at once and do not go near.
We keep far from them, and let the enemy draw near;
we keep them before us, and let the enemy have them at his back.
verses.living: Some situations are traps by their very shape: the job with no way out, the loan that compounds, the friendship that only runs downhill. Stay clear of them. Keep such ground in front of you, where you can see it, never behind you where it can swallow a retreat.

verses.en:
Where the march passes defiles and narrows,
ponds and pools, reeds and rushes,
mountain woods and tangled thickets,
search them with care, again and again:
these are the haunts of ambush and of spies.
verses.living: Read the fine print, above all the dense parts. In a contract, a plan or a promise, the tangled clauses are where surprises hide. Go over them twice, and ask a second pair of eyes to do the same.

verses.en:
When the enemy is near and quiet,
he trusts in strong ground.
When he is far off and throws down a challenge,
he wants you to advance.
When he camps on easy ground,
it serves some purpose of his.
verses.living: Ask why someone is behaving as they are. A competitor who is oddly calm may hold a strong position; someone provoking you from a distance may want you to overreach. Before you rise to the bait online or at work, ask what they gain if you answer.

verses.en:
The trees stir in numbers: he is coming.
Screens set among the grasses: he means to mislead.
Birds rise: an ambush.
Beasts bolt: a surprise attack.
Dust high and pointed: chariots coming.
Dust low and wide: foot soldiers coming.
Dust scattered in threads: men gathering firewood.
A little dust, moving to and fro: they are making camp.
verses.living: Small signs carry large meanings if you watch for them. A colleague's slower replies, a child's sudden silence about school, a shop that keeps cutting prices: each is dust on the horizon. Make a habit of naming what you notice and what it might mean.

verses.en:
Humble words and growing preparations: he will advance.
Bold words and a forward rush: he will withdraw.
Light chariots come out first to take the flanks: he is forming for battle.
Peace asked for with no pledge given: there is a plot.
Much running about and chariots drawn up: the hour is set.
Half advancing, half falling back: a lure.
verses.living: Watch actions over words. A supplier who apologises sweetly while quietly courting your best client is making a move; a rival's loud bluster may cover a retreat. An unexpected offer of peace with no terms attached deserves a courteous question: what is this for?

verses.en:
Men leaning on their weapons: they are hungry.
Water carriers drinking first: they are thirsty.
Gain in sight and no advance: they are worn out.
Birds gathering: the camp is empty.
Cries in the night: they are afraid.
Unrest in the ranks: the general lacks weight.
verses.living: These are the signs of a depleted group, and they hold for your own household and team as well. When people stop reaching for opportunities, they are tired, not lazy; when there is noise in the night, there is fear. Read them in yourself too: hunger, thirst, fatigue and fear all show before they are spoken.

verses.en:
Banners shifting about: disorder.
Officers short-tempered: they are weary.
Grain fed to the horses, the cattle killed for meat,
no cooking pots hung up,
no return to quarters:
this is a foe at the end of his road.
verses.living: Irritable managers are usually exhausted managers; answer the tiredness, not the tone. And when someone starts burning what they will need tomorrow, they have stopped planning for tomorrow. Give them a wide berth or a way out, never a fight.

verses.en:
Murmuring in huddles, speaking slow and soft to the men:
he has lost the ranks.
Rewards handed out again and again: he is at his wits' end.
Punishments again and again: he is hard pressed.
Harsh at first, then afraid of his own people:
the height of ineptitude.
Envoys arriving with gifts and apologies:
he wants a respite.
When troops come on in fury and face you,
yet long neither engage nor withdraw,
watch them with the utmost care.
verses.living: Leadership in trouble has a look: too many bonuses, too many reprimands, bluster followed by appeasement. Notice it in the organisations you join, and in yourself as a parent. And when someone is angry yet neither acts nor leaves, do not relax: something is being decided.

verses.en:
In war, more is not better.
Only do not advance on force alone;
it is enough to gather your strength,
take the enemy's measure,
and win people to you.
But whoever takes no thought
and makes light of the enemy
will surely be taken.
verses.living: You rarely need more resources; you need focus, an accurate reading of the problem, and the right people beside you. A small team that understands its market beats a large one that underestimates it. Contempt for a challenge is the surest way to lose to it.

verses.en:
Punish soldiers before they are bound to you,
and they will not submit;
unsubmitting, they are hard to use.
Once they are bound to you, if punishments are not carried out,
they cannot be used at all.
So command them with civility
and bring them into line with firmness:
this is called the sure way.
verses.living: Earn trust before you correct. A new manager who opens with reprimands breeds resentment; one who builds rapport and then never follows through breeds drift. Warmth first, standards always: the same holds for parenting and for your own habits.

verses.en:
When orders are steadily carried out in training the people,
the people submit.
When orders are not steadily carried out,
the people do not.
Orders steadily honoured
show that leader and people have found each other.
verses.living: Consistency is what gives words their weight. If you say the phones go away at dinner, they must go away every night, not only when you are in the mood. Small promises kept daily build the trust that larger requests will later rely on.

verses.en:
Sunzi said:
Ground takes six forms:
open, entangling, divided,
narrow, steep and distant.
Where we can go and they can come,
it is called open.
On open ground, be first to take the high and sunlit side,
keep the supply roads clear,
and battle will favour you.
verses.living: Some places give everyone easy access: a crowded market, an open job posting. There the advantage goes to whoever arrives early, takes the best position and keeps a steady supply. On open ground, speed and provision count for more than cleverness.

verses.en:
Where you can go but hardly return,
it is called entangling.
On entangling ground,
if the enemy is unready, go out and win.
If he is ready and you go out and fail,
there is no road back: no advantage there.
verses.living: Some commitments are easy to enter and hard to undo: a mortgage, a long contract, a public announcement. Before stepping in, ask whether you would still succeed if the other side were ready for you. If not, the cost of failure includes the road home.

verses.en:
Where neither we nor they gain by moving out first,
it is called divided.
On divided ground,
though the enemy dangles a gain before us,
we do not go out.
We draw off and leave,
and when half his force has come out, strike:
there is the advantage.
verses.living: In some stand-offs the first mover loses: the first to name a price, the first to escalate a family quarrel. When neither side gains by moving, step back and let the other come forward. Patience here is not weakness; it is position.

verses.en:
On narrow ground, if we are there first,
we must fill the pass and wait for the enemy.
If he is there first and has filled it, do not follow;
if he has not filled it, go in.
On steep ground, if we are there first,
we must hold the high and sunlit side and wait.
If the enemy is there first,
draw off and leave; do not follow.
verses.living: In a narrow niche, occupy it fully or not at all. If a competitor already serves it completely, look elsewhere; if they serve it thinly, there is room. On steep ground, a height someone else already commands, do not climb against them: find another hill.

verses.en:
On distant ground, where strength is matched,
it is hard to provoke a battle,
and to fight brings no advantage.
These six are the ways of the ground.
They are the general's weightiest charge;
they must be studied.
verses.living: When the distance is long and the sides evenly matched, picking a fight costs everyone. Think of a lawsuit over a small sum, a feud with a distant relative. Not every disagreement is worth the journey. Studying the ground includes knowing which ground to leave alone.

verses.en:
So armies may flee, go slack, sink,
crumble, fall into chaos, or be routed.
These six are not calamities sent by heaven;
they are the general's faults.
verses.living: When a project fails, it is tempting to blame bad luck, the economy, the weather. Sunzi refuses that comfort. Begin any review of a failure with the question: what part of this was mine?

verses.en:
When strength is equal and one is flung against ten,
that is flight.
Strong soldiers, weak officers:
that is slackness.
Strong officers, weak soldiers:
that is sinking.
When senior officers are angry and will not submit,
meet the enemy with resentment and fight on their own account,
and the general does not know their abilities:
that is collapse.
verses.living: Mismatches break teams: impossible odds, capable people under weak managers, driving managers over an untrained team, senior people pursuing private quarrels. Ask which mismatch is present where you work, and mend the structure before you blame the people.

verses.en:
When the general is weak and without severity,
his teaching and guidance unclear,
officers and men without settled duties,
the ranks drawn up every which way:
that is chaos.
When the general cannot gauge the enemy,
sends few against many, the weak against the strong,
and has no chosen vanguard:
that is rout.
These six are the ways of defeat.
They are the general's weightiest charge;
they must be studied.
verses.living: Clear roles and an honest reading of the challenge prevent most disasters. Before a family move or a product launch, make sure everyone knows their part. Match the task to the strength you actually have, and put your best people at the front.

verses.en:
The form of the ground is an ally to arms.
To gauge the enemy and shape the victory,
to reckon the hazards and narrows, the far and the near:
this is the way of the superior general.
Who knows this and fights will surely win;
who knows it not and fights will surely lose.
verses.living: Circumstances are not only obstacles; understood, they are help. A writer who knows when she works best, where she is undisturbed and how long a draft truly takes is using the ground. Map the terrain of your own goals: what is near, what is far, and where the narrow places lie.

verses.en:
So if the course of battle promises victory,
fight, though the ruler says do not.
If the course of battle does not promise victory,
do not fight, though the ruler says you must.
The general who advances without seeking fame
and withdraws without dodging blame,
whose one concern is to protect the people
and to serve his sovereign's true good,
is the treasure of the realm.
verses.living: Integrity sometimes means telling a boss or a client that their plan will fail, and accepting the cost of saying so. Do it not for credit and not to cover yourself, but to protect the people the plan will touch. Such people are rare, and every organisation knows their worth.

verses.en:
Look on your soldiers as infants,
and they will go with you into the deepest gorge.
Look on them as your beloved sons,
and they will stand with you to the death.
But be generous and unable to direct them,
loving and unable to command them,
let them run riot and be unable to order them,
and they are like spoiled children:
of no use at all.
verses.living: Care is the root of loyalty, but care without standards breeds entitlement. Whether raising children or leading a team, be warm and be clear: protect people fiercely and still ask real things of them.

verses.en:
To know your troops can strike
but not that the enemy cannot be struck
is half a victory.
To know the enemy can be struck
but not that your troops cannot strike
is half a victory.
To know the enemy can be struck
and your troops can strike,
but not that the ground forbids the fight,
is half a victory.
verses.living: Half-knowledge is a coin toss. You may know your product is good but not that the market is closed. You may know the market is open but not that your team is exhausted; know both and misjudge the moment. Check all three before you commit.

verses.en:
So one who truly knows war
moves without confusion
and acts without running dry.
Hence it is said:
know the other and know yourself,
and victory carries no danger;
know heaven and know earth,
and victory knows no end.
verses.living: Understanding the other person, yourself, the timing and the circumstances is the whole of good judgement. Before a career move, write a paragraph on each: the employer, yourself, the moment, the field. Wherever a paragraph comes out thin, there is your homework.

chapters.title_en: Nine Grounds, and No Way Back

verses.en:
Master Sun said:
In the use of armies
there is scattering ground,
light ground,
contested ground,
open ground,
ground where highways meet,
heavy ground,
broken ground,
enclosed ground,
and death ground.
verses.living: Before acting, name the ground you are on. A new job in its first month, a negotiation where both sides want the same prize, a project you cannot abandon. Each asks for a different posture. Most mistakes come from making the right move on the wrong ground.

verses.en:
When a lord fights on his own soil,
that is scattering ground.
When you have entered another's land, but not deeply,
that is light ground.
Ground that profits us if we take it
and profits them if they do
is contested ground.
Ground where we can go
and they can come
is open ground.
verses.living: Scattering ground is why big decisions made amid the comforts of home so often drift: ease pulls attention in every direction. Light ground is the shallow commitment, the evening class you could still drop at no cost. Notice which ground leaves your resolve thin, and arrange things so it thickens.

verses.en:
Where the borders of three states touch,
and whoever arrives first
wins the allegiance of all under heaven,
that is ground where highways meet.
When you have gone deep into another's land,
with many walled towns at your back,
that is heavy ground.
verses.living: Crossroads ground is where many networks meet: a trade fair, a new professional circle, the friend who knows everyone. There, arriving early and making allies matters more than fighting anyone. Heavy ground is where you are already committed, three years into a career or a mortgage, and retreat would cost more than going on.

verses.en:
Mountain forest, steep defiles, marsh and fen,
every road that is hard to travel:
that is broken ground.
Where the way in is narrow,
the way back winds,
and a few of theirs can strike many of ours:
that is enclosed ground.
Where swift battle means survival
and delay means ruin:
that is death ground.
verses.living: Enclosed ground is the meeting where you are outnumbered and the exit is awkward. Death ground is the deadline that cannot slip, the bill that must be paid this month. On death ground, deliberation itself becomes the danger. Recognise it, and act at once with your whole weight.

This is a short manual of fit: each situation has its one right verb. In a shallow commitment, do not linger; on a field everyone wants, do not charge in head first; when hemmed in, think rather than push. Write your present situation on a card and ask which verb it calls for.

Tangled problems yield when you keep their parts from feeding one another. A messy renovation, a family dispute, a budget in disarray: take one strand at a time. And keep the closing rule near: move when it serves the purpose, stop when it does not, never merely because momentum carries you.

verses.en:
Someone asked:
"The enemy comes in great numbers and good order.
How shall we meet him?"
I said:
"First take hold of what he holds dear,
and he will listen."
verses.living: When facing someone stronger and well prepared, find out what matters most to them. In a negotiation it may be their timetable or their reputation; speaking to that earns attention faster than pressure ever will. Know what a person treasures and you know where the conversation really is.

verses.en:
Speed is the heart of war:
ride on what others have not yet reached,
go by the road they never imagined,
strike where they have set no guard.
verses.living: Openings favour the quick. When a role appears, a market turns, or an idea ripens, the one who moves while others are still discussing usually takes it. Look too for the road nobody watches: the overlooked client, the unglamorous skill.

Going deep focuses you as dabbling never can: the writer who has told everyone about the book, the founder who has left the safe job. But depth needs tending: rest your team, feed them well, bank your energy. Concentration joined to conserved strength is what makes you hard to predict.

A bridge burnt on purpose can set you free. Some people enter the marathon, publish the launch date, or tell their friends they have stopped smoking. They often find a courage they lacked while every option stayed open. Use this sparingly, and on yourself first: remove the easy exit only from goals you truly want.

verses.en:
So such troops are watchful without drilling,
give without being asked,
are close without being bound,
keep faith without being ordered.
Forbid omens, clear away doubts,
and to the death they will not turn aside.
verses.living: A team that truly shares one fate needs fewer rules: people cover for each other without being told. The leader's task is to remove the rumours and second-guessing that sap them, the vague memo, the half-told plan. Clear the doubt and commitment largely looks after itself.

verses.en:
Our soldiers keep no wealth to spare,
not because they despise goods;
no life to spare,
not because they hate long years.
On the day the order goes out,
those sitting soak their collars with tears,
those lying down have tears crossing their cheeks.
But throw them where there is nowhere to go
and they have the courage of Zhuan Zhu and Cao Gui.
verses.living: Courage is not the absence of fear or of love for life: the soldiers weep, and then they go. Before an operation, a resignation, or a hard conversation with an ageing parent, let yourself feel the grief fully. Then step forward anyway; tears and resolve are not opposites.

verses.en:
The skilled commander is like the shuairan,
the snake of Mount Chang.
Strike its head, and the tail comes;
strike its tail, and the head comes;
strike its middle, and head and tail come together.
Someone asked:
"Can an army be made like the shuairan?"
I said:
"It can."
verses.living: A healthy household or team answers as one body: when one part is struck, the others come without a meeting. Build that by making sure everyone understands the whole, not only their own slice. When the kitchen floods, it matters less that one person knows where the stopcock is than that everyone does.

verses.en:
The people of Wu and the people of Yue hate each other;
yet put them in one boat, crossing a river,
and let a storm come:
they will save each other
like left hand and right.
verses.living: Shared danger makes partners of rivals. Two departments that bicker unite in a crisis; neighbours who never speak bail out the same flooded street. If you want cooperation, help people see the boat they are already in together.

verses.en:
So tethering the horses and burying the wheels
is not enough to rely on.
To make courage level, as if in one body,
is the way of governing;
to get the best of both hard and soft
is the pattern of the ground.
The skilled commander leads them hand in hand
as though they were one person:
they have no other way.
verses.living: Binding people with contracts and penalties is weak glue. Real unity comes from fair leadership and from using each person's nature, the firm and the gentle alike. When people see that the situation itself asks for unity, they join hands without being made to.

verses.en:
The general's work:
still, and so unfathomable;
upright, and so in good order.
He can keep his soldiers' eyes and ears unknowing,
so that they do not know.
He changes his arrangements, alters his plans,
so none can recognise them;
shifts his camp, takes winding roads,
so none can anticipate him.
verses.living: Calm and integrity are a leader's first tools: a still mind is hard to read and hard to rattle. Not every half-formed plan needs announcing; sharing too early breeds anxiety and leaks. Discretion is not deceit: tell people what they need, when it helps them act.

verses.en:
When he fixes the hour with them,
it is like climbing high and kicking away the ladder.
He leads them deep into the lands of the lords
and releases the trigger:
burns the boats, smashes the cooking pots,
drives them like a flock of sheep,
this way and then that,
and no one knows where they are going.
To gather the whole host
and throw it into danger:
this is the general's work.
The changes of the nine grounds,
the advantage of bending and stretching,
the pattern of the human heart:
these must be examined.
verses.living: Some commitments only work once the ladder is gone: notice handed in, venue booked, second car sold. Yet the closing lines matter most: know when to bend and when to stretch, and study how people actually feel. Boldness without understanding of the human heart is merely recklessness.

verses.en:
The way of the invader:
go deep and you are single-minded,
stay shallow and you scatter.
To leave your country and cross the border with an army:
that is cut-off ground.
Where roads run out in four directions:
ground where highways meet.
Gone in deep: heavy ground.
Gone in shallow: light ground.
Strongholds behind, a narrow pass in front:
enclosed ground.
Nowhere to go:
death ground.
verses.living: Half-measures scatter energy. Learning a language in five-minute app sessions is shallow ground; a month living abroad is deep. Decide which you are doing, because the shallow version brings most of the costs and few of the gains.

Different seasons of life ask for different care. In a scattered time, choose one aim. In a demanding new role, keep supplies of sleep and money flowing. In a tight corner, close off the tempting escape routes that only drain attention. Name the season, and choose its one task.

Before moving to a new city or a new firm, find local guides. Look for the colleague of ten years, the neighbour who knows which schools are good. Pride makes us skip this step. Asking those who know the terrain is not weakness; it is the first act of competence.

verses.en:
When a hegemon's army attacks a great state,
that state cannot gather its people;
when his weight bears on the enemy,
the enemy's alliances cannot come together.
So he does not scramble for every alliance under heaven,
nor feed the power of others,
but trusts in his own resources
and bears down on the enemy;
so their cities can be taken,
their state overthrown.
verses.living: Some people spend all their energy courting others, building everyone's standing but their own. Real strength is quieter: develop your own craft, savings and judgement so that you need not please the whole room. Self-reliance makes your presence felt without a campaign.

verses.en:
Give rewards beyond the rules,
issue orders beyond the usual codes,
and you can wield the whole army
as if directing one person.
Engage them with the task,
do not explain with words;
engage them with the gain,
do not tell them of the harm.
verses.living: Exceptional moments may need exceptional recognition: the thanks no one expected, the reward outside the yearly review. People are often moved more by doing than by speeches, so give a team the task and its purpose rather than a lecture. Read for life, the last line warns against heaping every worry on people who first need momentum. It never says to hide risks they have a right to know.

verses.en:
Throw them into ground where they would perish,
and they survive;
sink them in death ground,
and they live.
Only when people have fallen into harm
can they turn it into victory.
verses.living: Crises often bring out abilities that comfort hides. The redundancy that forces a long-postponed change, the illness that clarifies priorities: these are not to be sought, but when they come, remember this line. Danger can be the place where you finally become decisive.

verses.en:
The business of war
lies in carefully going along with the enemy's intent,
then turning all your force one way
to strike down his general a thousand li off.
This is called achieving things by skill.
verses.living: Instead of opposing someone head-on, first follow their direction attentively: let the client finish explaining, let the toddler's storm run its course. Once you see where their energy is going, gather yours on the one decisive point. Skill is mostly attention, then focus.

verses.en:
So on the day war is resolved,
close the passes, break the tallies,
let no envoys through;
in the hall of the ancestors, be stern,
and settle the matter.
When the enemy leaves a door ajar,
rush in at once.
Go first for what he holds dear,
and keep the hour of meeting hidden.
Keep to the inked line, yet move with the enemy,
to decide the battle.
verses.living: Once a decision is truly made, stop reopening it: close the channels of endless debate and turn the plan into action. Then stay alert for the opening, the reply that shows the door is ajar. Hold your principles like a carpenter's line, but let the situation set the rhythm.

verses.en:
So at first, be quiet as a girl in her chamber,
and the enemy opens his door;
afterwards, be swift as a hare let loose,
and the enemy is too late to resist.
verses.living: Quiet preparation, then sudden speed: the writer who drafts in private and publishes in a burst, the athlete who trains unseen. Keep plans soft-spoken until they are ready, then move without hesitation. Stillness and speed are one strategy in two phases.

chapters.title_en: Fire, and the Cooling of Anger

verses.living: Powerful tools need prepared conditions. A product launch, a proposal, a public apology: each lands only if the materials are gathered beforehand. Lay the kindling quietly, long before you need the flame.

verses.en:
There is a season for setting fire
and a day for raising it.
The season is when the weather is dry;
the days are when the moon stands
in the Winnowing Basket, the Wall, the Wings or the Carriage.
These four lodges
mark the days when wind rises.
verses.living: Timing is part of the act. Ask for the rise after a win, not after a bad quarter. Start a new habit at a natural turning point, not in the middle of a crisis. Learn the seasons and winds of the people around you and your efforts will catch.

verses.en:
In every fire attack
you must answer the five changes of fire.
When fire breaks out inside their camp,
respond early from outside.
If fire breaks out yet their soldiers stay calm,
wait, do not attack;
let the fire reach its height,
then follow up if you can,
and stop if you cannot.
verses.living: When something you have started begins to work, watch the response before piling in. If a colleague stays calm after you raise a problem, do not escalate; wait and see what the calm means. Follow through where there is an opening, and let it go where there is none.

verses.en:
If fire can be set from outside,
do not wait for it within;
set it when the time is right.
When the fire is upwind,
do not attack from downwind.
Wind that blows long by day
falls still at night.
Every army must know the five changes of fire
and keep watch by reckoning the days.
verses.living: Do not stand downwind of your own fire: a harsh email can blow back on its sender, a rumour can turn on whoever started it. Notice which way things are blowing before you set anything going. And daytime winds drop at night: so does most outrage, given time.

verses.en:
Fire as an aid to attack is clear-sighted;
water as an aid to attack is strong.
Water can cut an enemy off
but cannot take what is his.
To win battles and take what you attack
yet fail to secure what you have won
bodes ill:
its name is wasteful lingering.
verses.living: Winning is not finishing. The qualification earned but never used, the deal signed but never implemented, the diet abandoned the day the target is reached: all are wasteful lingering. Plan the follow-through as carefully as the push.

Anger is the worst reason to start anything: the furious reply, the vengeful lawsuit, the job quit in a rage. Before acting, ask three questions: is there real gain, will I truly secure it, is there real necessity? If not, the strongest move is to wait.

verses.en:
Anger may turn back to gladness,
resentment back to delight;
but a fallen state cannot be raised again,
nor can the dead be brought back to life.
So the clear-sighted ruler is careful,
the good general is wary:
this is the way to keep the state at peace
and the army whole.
verses.living: Moods pass; some consequences do not. Words flung in a quarrel with a partner, trust broken with a child: these may not come back as easily as your temper settles. When your blood is up, remember that the feeling is temporary and the act may be permanent.

verses.en:
Master Sun said:
Raise an army of a hundred thousand,
send it a thousand li to war,
and the people's outlay and the state's expense
come to a thousand pieces of gold a day.
Within the borders and beyond there is upheaval;
people drop exhausted on the roads;
seven hundred thousand households
cannot tend their work.
verses.living: Large undertakings carry hidden costs far beyond the visible budget. A house move, a lawsuit, a long feud at work: count the hours, the sleep, the people pulled from their own lives. Once the full cost is seen, good information looks cheap.

verses.en:
Armies face each other for years
to contend for a single day's victory;
so to begrudge rank, salary and a hundred pieces of gold,
and stay ignorant of the enemy's condition,
is the height of inhumanity.
Such a one is no general of men,
no support to his ruler,
no master of victory.
verses.living: Stinginess about knowledge is false economy. Skipping the survey before buying a house, refusing to pay for advice before signing, building before asking a single customer. Each saves a small sum and risks a large one. Spending to understand is an act of care for everyone who would bear the cost of your mistakes.

verses.en:
What lets the clear-sighted ruler and the worthy general
move and overcome others,
and achieve what the many cannot,
is knowing first.
Knowing first cannot be drawn from ghosts and spirits,
cannot be inferred from likenesses,
cannot be confirmed by measuring the heavens;
it must come from people,
people who know the enemy's condition.
verses.living: Foresight comes from people, not horoscopes or hunches. Before a career change, talk to three people already doing the work; before investing, talk to someone inside the industry. The answer you need is usually walking around in someone else's head.

verses.en:
There are five kinds of go-between:
the local, the inside,
the turned, the doomed,
and the one who returns.
When all five are at work
and no one knows their ways,
this is called the divine web,
the sovereign's treasure.
verses.living: Good information arrives through many channels at once: friends, figures, customers, critics, your own eyes. When they all work quietly together, you seem to know things before they happen. Build several channels rather than trusting one.

verses.en:
Local agents:
you use people of the enemy's own district.
Inside agents:
you use his officials.
Turned agents:
you use the enemy's own spies.
Doomed agents:
you stage false matters abroad,
let our agent learn of them,
and have him carry them to the enemy's spies.
Returning agents:
they come back and report.
verses.living: Read through a modern lens, this is a map of how information travels. It moves through locals, insiders, people who carry it both ways, and those who come back to tell. Notice too that some news reaching you was planted on purpose, through a messenger who sincerely believes it. Always ask who benefits from what you are being told.

verses.en:
In all the army's affairs
none are closer to the commander than his agents,
no rewards richer,
no business more secret.
Without sagely wisdom you cannot use agents;
without humaneness and rightness you cannot direct them;
without fine subtlety you cannot draw the truth from them.
Subtle! Subtle!
There is nothing where agents are not used.
If a secret matter is heard before it is launched,
the agent and all he told must die.
verses.living: Those who bring you the truth deserve your closest trust and your best reward: the honest friend, the employee who flags the problem early. Using information well needs wisdom, decency and a feel for nuance. And confidences matter: a leaked plan or a betrayed secret can end a relationship outright.

verses.en:
Whatever army you wish to strike,
whatever city to attack,
whatever man to strike down,
you must first know the names
of the commander who holds it,
his aides, his ushers, his gatekeepers, his household staff.
Have our agents seek them all out.
verses.living: Before a major pitch, learn who is actually in the room. That means not only the decision-maker but also the assistant who keeps the diary and the adviser whose opinion counts. Organisations are made of people with names. Know them, respect them, and doors open.

The critic who probes your work is a source, not only a threat. Treat them generously, listen, give them a seat: the harshest reviewer can become your best informant about what is wrong. People who came looking for your weakness can end by helping you mend it.

One well-placed relationship unlocks many others: a mentor who introduces you, a former competitor who knows the market from inside. Invest most in the connection that opens the rest. Generosity to the person who bridges two worlds repays itself many times over.

verses.en:
Of old, when Yin arose,
Yi Zhi had served in Xia;
when Zhou arose,
Lü Ya had served in Yin.
So only the clear-sighted ruler and worthy general
who can make those of highest wisdom their go-betweens
will achieve great things.
This is the crux of war,
what the whole army leans on when it moves.
verses.living: The finest understanding comes from the wisest people, especially those who have lived on both sides of a divide. Seek advisers who have worked where you want to go and also understand where you stand now. Their insight is worth more than any heap of raw data.
